900.author: yuanzhou75
900.body:
## Summary

Registering a GLM (or other OpenAI-compatible) model with `apiVariant: "deepseek"` makes the runtime inject thinking-control parameters (`enable_thinking`, `reasoning`, `thinking.type`) into model requests. Some OpenAI-compatible gateways reject these with 400:

```
BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'Unsupported gateway parameters: enable_thinking, reasoning', 'type': 'model_gateway_error'}}
```

and separately, for the image-modality warmup probe:

```
BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'images are not supported by this gateway', 'type': 'model_gateway_error'}}
```

Main text/chat completions still succeed, but the housekeeping image probe fails on every start, leaving `image_input=unknown`.

## Reproduction

1. Register a model via `POST /api/models` with `apiProtocol: "openai-chat-completions"`, `apiVariant: "deepseek"`, and a GLM OpenAI-compatible `baseUrl`.
2. Start the stack and watch the JiuwenSwarm llm log for the image warmup probe ("What color is this image? Reply with one word.").

## Observed behaviour

- `llm_call_error … BadRequestError: 400 - Unsupported gateway parameters: enable_thinking, reasoning`
- `llm_call_error … images are not supported by this gateway`
- Warmup records `image_input=unknown (not cached)`.

## Expected behaviour

- Thinking-control params should only be injected for dialects/gateways that accept them, or a gateway rejection of those extra params should be tolerated rather than erroring the warmup.
- An "images not supported" rejection should be recorded cleanly as "image input not supported", not surfaced as a repeated 400 error.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery local stack on WSL2 (Ubuntu), JiuwenSwarm backend.
- Model: glm-5.3-flash, baseUrl `https://yibuapi.com/v1`, apiVariant `deepseek`.
- Main chat completion works (greeting + idea-tree runs succeeded); only the image probe is affected.
900.title: [Bug]: deepseek API variant sends enable_thinking/reasoning params that some OpenAI-compatible gateways reject

903.author: HugoXK
903.body:
## Summary

**Scope update (2026-11-05): this issue now tracks D2 only.** D1 is not a deferrable gap — `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA` bypass the predicate that #890 itself adds, so the failure class that pull request removes is still reachable through the stream form. That makes #890 incomplete rather than lightly scoped, so D1 is being fixed inside #890: its `F1` review thread was reopened and the predicate change (split the stem on `:` as well as `.`) plus the `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA` cases land on that branch. D2 stays here because it is a separate, pre-existing portability gap (a POSIX host creates a file the host can open and Windows cannot), not the device-write failure #890 removes.

The Windows-reserved-name guard added in #890 refuses `CON/notes.txt`, `nul.dir/x.csv` and `notes/CON.txt`, but one input form still produces an unportable file. Both `F1` and `F2` were raised as medium review threads on #890; `F2` is the one tracked here.

## D1 — `nul:stream` / `con:$DATA` — **moved into #890, not tracked here**

Kept for the record only; the fix lands in #890 itself (see the scope update above).

- **Where:** `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts:479` (predicate added by #890)
- **Cause:** the stem is everything before the first dot, so `nul:stream` keeps its colon (`nul:stream`), the reserved-name regex misses it, and the predicate returns `false`.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"nul:stream"}` or `{"path":"con:$DATA"}`.
- **Observed:** on POSIX the route answers `201` and creates a file Windows cannot open; on Windows the write targets the device — the exact failure class #890 removes, still reachable.
- **Expected:** the request is refused with `400`, naming the offending segment, exactly as `CON/notes.txt` is today.
- **Suggested fix:** split the stem on `:` as well as `.` — e.g. `name.split(/[.:]/)[0]?.replace(/[. ]+$/, "")` — plus `nul:stream` and `con:$DATA` cases in `WSP-005`.

## D2 — `CON\notes.txt`: the segment walk splits on the host separator only

- **Where:** `services/api/src/http/index.ts:3815`
- **Cause:** `relative(workspaceRoot, target).split(sep)` splits on `/` on Linux, so `CON\notes.txt` stays one segment, the stem reads `CON\notes`, and the predicate allows it. The predicate and the route comment both claim the rule is platform-independent.
- **Failing input:** `POST /api/sessions/:id/files` with `{"path":"CON\\notes.txt"}` against a Linux server.
- **Observed:** `201` and a workspace file literally named `CON\notes.txt`; the same request is refused on a Windows host, so the answer depends on which platform serves it.
- **Expected:** refused on every host, with one test case alongside the existing `CON/notes.txt` one.
- **Suggested fix:** split on both separators (`relative(...).split(/[\\/]+/)`) and/or refuse `\` inside a segment.

## Verification

- Both defects are reproducible from the reproduction steps above against #890's head `c4fb33d4`; neither is a wording question.
- Acceptance: both inputs answer `400` with the offending segment named, the existing `WSP-005` cases stay green, and the guard's claim of being platform-independent holds on Linux and Windows.

Owner: ScienceDiscovery Dev-Lead
Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Dev-Lead
903.title: fix(api): split the device-name segment walk on both separators (`CON\notes.txt` on a POSIX host)

909.author: HugoXK
909.body:
## Summary

`ST` fails on a clean `main` because the pinned Python runtime is fetched from `astral-sh/python-build-standalone` and that download either answers `504` or streams at 9–31 KB/s, far past the 5-minute `execFile` cap in the test. It fails before any code under test runs, so it is not attributable to the PR whose run turns red — but it does turn `merge-gate` red, which is the one required check in this repository, so it blocks merges.

Current instance: `#678` (tip `5ad9b21b6aeb5d7f30556de8ddafc07d1246d85e`) is approved and otherwise green except `ST`.

## Where

- Test: `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts::a user initializes the pinned release into an empty installation and completes a real Evolve task@linux/amd64`
- Downloader: `scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs`
- Asset: `https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz` — `34,184,519` bytes

## CI evidence

Run [`41999191976`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41999191976), job `ST` `127150383484` (`2026-11-05T09:04:19Z` → `09:09:17Z`): `{"status":"FAIL","planned":51,"executed":51,"passed":50,"failed":1}`, the only red identity is the test above, first line:

```
Download failed (504): https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone/releases/download/20260805/cpython-3.12.13+20260805-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only_stripped.tar.gz
```

## Control: the same case on a clean `main`

`main` at `7057aaf65f2c81d0b0af64a449d9259c62128673`, tracked tree clean, dependencies installed and built the same way, no branch of `#678` present:

- `node scripts/binary-release/fetch-runtime.mjs --runtime python --arch x86_64 --output … --cache …` → **exit 124** (killed at a 300 s cap; it had written 0 bytes to disk, because the script reads the whole archive into memory before writing).
- `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "pinned release" test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` → **exit 1** after **301 s** (`duration_ms: 300128`), i.e. it hit the same `execFile` 5-minute cap with the same command and the same URL.

So the same case fails on `main` without the change under review.

## Observed throughput for that asset

| Reading | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `curl -sI` (same URL) | `HTTP/2 302` |
| `curl -sL -r 0-1048575` (1 MiB range) | `206`, `1,048,576` bytes in `33.48 s` → `31,322 B/s` |
| `curl -L` (full, 45 s cap) | `200`, `818,498` of `34,184,519` bytes in `45 s` → `18,185 B/s` |
| bare `node fetch` | `status 200` in `1.1 s`, then 0 bytes for 60 s before abort |
| independent samples of the same URL, three machines | `9,445` / `25,735` / `18,312` B/s |

At `9–31 KB/s` the `34 MB` asset needs roughly **18 to 60 minutes**, while the test allows 5.

## It is not deterministic

Fifteen minutes before the red run, the same case passed in merge-group run [`41997396390`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997396390) (`2026-11-05T08:52:58Z` → `08:53:41Z`, `42.6 s`). `main`'s own `ST` was green in run [`41997392457`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41997392457) (`08:52Z`). So the failure tracks the download path degrading, not a fixed defect in the test.

## Why this is worth a fix rather than a retry

`merge-gate` is the only required status check here, and `ST` is one of the jobs it aggregates, so any PR can be blocked for a reason that has nothing to do with its diff, and a re-run only helps if the CDN happens to recover. Retries also cost a full `ST` cycle (≈5 minutes each time) and cannot be triggered by contributors: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` both answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` for a non-member token.

## Options, in the order we would pick them

1. **Cache the pinned runtime between runs** (keyed by the asset version), so the network is used once per version instead of on every `ST` run.
2. **Verify against a mirror first** and fall back to the GitHub release, or honour `fetch-runtime.mjs`'s resume/cache path when a partial download exists instead of restarting from byte 0.
3. **Fail fast and name the cause**: if the download cannot reach a minimum rate within N seconds, fail with a message that says "external asset download too slow", so the red check is self-explanatory.
4. If none of the above is wanted now, an explicit **retry/exemption policy for `ST` on this identity** would at least stop it blocking unrelated PRs.

If the project prefers that this be reported differently, say so and we will follow that shape instead.
909.title: [Bug] ST fails on clean main: the pinned Python runtime download times out (504 or 9-31 KB/s) before any test code runs

910.author: HugoXK
910.body:
## Summary

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts` gives its fault injection a wall-clock budget of about `200 ms` (`200` iterations at `1 ms`). On a busy runner that budget is exhausted before the injected fault lands, the case fails with `Timed out waiting for local fault injection`, and because `UT` is one of the jobs `merge-gate` aggregates, an unrelated pull request turns red on the only required status check in this repository.

Two pull requests were hit by the same identity in two different time windows today, and the same file passes in a normal run.

## Failing identity

```text
packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts::parallel 429 callers share cooldown, drain their queue and do not retry inside one slot@linux/amd64
message: "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"
```

## Evidence

**Hit 1 — `#872`**, `UT` job `126735548839`, run [`41875320473`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41875320473), read from the job's uploaded `ut-results` artifact (`group-227/worker-1-events.jsonl`; the job log itself only carries `Run`/`Done` lines). Group summary `planned 16 / executed 16 / passed 15 / failed 1`; whole layer `planned 6279 / executed 6279 / passed 6278 / failed 1`.

**Hit 2 — `#878`**, `UT` job `126741018427`, same identity, another window.

**Control — the same file passing**, `UT` job `126822084143` (`2026-11-04T19:54:21Z`): `Run 229/555: packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts (16)` → `Done (6210ms)`, layer `{"status":"PASS","planned":6281,"passed":6281,"failed":0}`.

Neither pull request touches `packages/data-source`: `#872` changes four files under `apps/web`, `#878` changes `apps/web` only. So the failing identity is unreachable from either diff.

## Cause

`packages/data-source/src/source-health.test.ts:98-101` polls for the first of 12 concurrent callers to observe the injected fault:

```ts
// ~200 iterations × 1 ms ≈ 200 ms total
```

When the event loop is loaded (parallel `UT` workers, coverage instrumentation), `200 ms` is not enough for the fault to be observed, and the wait falls through to `assert.fail("Timed out waiting for local fault injection")`. The product behaviour is correct; the budget is what fails.

## Effect

Any pull request can be blocked by this, and a re-run only helps if the runner happens to be less loaded. Contributors cannot re-run: `POST /actions/jobs/{id}/rerun` and `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` answer `403 Must have admin rights to Repository` to a non-member token. So the only currently available recovery is asking a maintainer.

## Options

1. **Replace the fixed budget with a deadline** (for example `waitFor` with a `10 s` timeout and a short poll interval), so a loaded runner still passes and a genuinely missing fault still fails quickly enough.
2. **Wait on the event rather than polling** — if the injection can expose a promise or an emitter, awaiting it removes the timing assumption entirely.
3. If the current budget is deliberate, document the expected runner load and treat the red as a known flake; then it should not be able to block `merge-gate` for unrelated changes.

We can prepare option 1 as a pull request if that is the preferred shape; tell us which option you want and we will follow that instead of choosing for you.
910.title: [Bug] UT flake: source-health.test.ts waits only ~200 ms for the injected fault, so a busy runner fails "Timed out waiting for local fault injection"

911.author: yuanzhou75
911.body:
## Summary

When a research agent writes files to its workspace during a run (e.g. `analysis.py`, `cleaned-data.csv`, SVG figures, `results.json`, helper scripts), those files are **not registered as artifacts** in the project's artifact list (`GET /api/projects/:id/artifacts`). Only files that were explicitly uploaded by the user before the run (e.g. `clinical_trial.csv`) appear as artifacts.

This means the user cannot download, preview, or manage the agent's output files through the artifact panel — they are stranded in the session workspace.

## Observed

During RR-02 (clinical trial re-analysis) on master `9e9d83d5` + WSL2:

- The agent wrote **8 files** to its session workspace:
  - `analysis.py` (41 KB)
  - `cleaned-data.csv` (4.6 KB)
  - `figures/fig1_endpoint_by_group.svg` (14.6 KB)
  - `figures/fig2_baseline_vs_endpoint.svg` (12.8 KB)
  - `figures/fig3_forest_plot.svg` (5.9 KB)
  - `figures/fig4_qq_residuals.svg` (12.9 KB)
  - `results/results.json` (6.1 KB)
  - `scripts/clinical_stats.py` (10.8 KB)

- `GET /api/projects/:id/artifacts` returned only **1 artifact**: `clinical_trial.csv` (the user's pre-run upload).

- The agent's output files were verifiably present in the session workspace (confirmed by direct filesystem access and by re-running `analysis.py` to reproduce identical results).

## Run identifiers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Run ID | `9e7a4a73-680` (cancelled after 30 min driver timeout, but workspace files were written) |
| Session ID | `3aece6df-fbca-410b-9eca-9f80b4c48da3` |
| Project ID | `56900995-89be-4290-a24b-b89f76ccbd82` |
| Created at | 2026-11-05T09:34:07Z |
| Model | glm-5.3-flash via yibuapi.com |
| SD commit | `9e9d83d5` (master) |

## Reproduction

1. Start the local stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local`.
2. Create a project/session, set `approvalMode: always_allow`.
3. Upload a CSV (`POST /api/sessions/:sid/workspace/upload`).
4. Send a data-analysis prompt that instructs the agent to write output files (e.g. `analysis.py`, `cleaned-data.csv`, figures, `results.json`).
5. Wait for the agent to write files to the workspace (observable via the session workspace filesystem).
6. Call `GET /api/projects/:pid/artifacts`.
7. Observe: only the uploaded CSV appears; the agent-written files are absent.

## Expected behaviour

Files written by the agent to the session workspace should be registered as project artifacts (or at minimum, surfaceable through the artifact panel) so the user can download, preview, and manage them without needing direct filesystem access.

The test guidance (§8.1) explicitly calls out "报告已写入工作区但未登记为产物" (report written to workspace but not registered as artifact) as a defect to look for.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu)
- SD commit: `9e9d83d5` (master, clean tree)
- JiuwenSwarm: `workswarm0.2.6`
- Model: `glm-5.3-flash` via yibuapi.com (OpenAI-compatible)
- API: `http://127.0.0.1:4310`, Runner: `4311`, Adapter: `4410`

## Reproducibility of the agent's analysis (verified)

As a side note, the agent's `analysis.py` was re-run in a clean directory and produced **identical** results (exact match on all primary and sensitivity analysis numbers), confirming the agent's work was scientifically sound — the only defect is that its outputs are not surfaced as artifacts.
911.title: [Bug] Agent-written workspace files are not registered as project artifacts
